The grammar then reads the header keyword again, `classDiagram-v2` or `classDiagram`, not followed by a word character (see [The statement context](#the-statement-context)), and then a `newline` unit. class-declaration.comment: Rule 14 and the bounded keyword class enters the class context, which reads strings, whitespace, a member body and the shared rules until a line feed; } can also close a namespace. class.md#the-statement-context: **The direction line.** From the current position: a run of characters without line feeds, U+2028, or U+2029, the longest one that the rest can follow; then `direction`; then one or more whitespace characters, line feeds included; then one of `TB`, `BT`, `RL`, and `LR`; and then every character up to the next line feed, which is not included. The rule reads the characters before `direction` as a `direction-text` unit, `direction` as a `direction` unit, the value as a `direction-value` unit, and the characters after the value as another `direction-text` unit; a `direction-text` unit that would be empty or all whitespace is left out. mermaid.js does not read the `direction-text` units. The values are tried in the order given: if the line has `direction` followed by `TB` anywhere, the value is `TB`; otherwise `BT` is tried, and so on. For a value, the lexer takes the last `direction` of the run that it follows, and the unit ends at the end of the line on which the value stands. So `direction TB x direction TB` is read at its last `direction`, and `direction TB x` is a `direction-text` unit.
